title: The Year of Sorrow
hook: In one year he lost the wife who believed him first and the uncle who shielded him.

screens.text: **In one year, he lost the two people who had stood closest to him.** The wife who believed him first. The uncle who had shielded him since he was a boy.
**Khadijah dies.** Khadijah died about three years before the hijra, his move to Madinah [Bukhari 3896]. They had been married about 25 years [Qalam ep. 55; Yaqeen].
bubbles: She was the one who wrapped him up and comforted him on the night of Hira [Bukhari 3].

screens.title: What each of them gave him

cards.back: Comfort and belief on the night of Hira, and about 25 years of marriage [Bukhari 3; Yaqeen].
A home from the age of about eight, and protection for over forty years [IslamQA 20240; IslamQA 11575].

screens.text: **Abu Talib dies.** Around the same time, about ten years into his mission, his uncle Abu Talib died [IslamQA 11575; IslamQA 20240]. He never accepted Islam, yet the Prophet ﷺ loved him.
bubbles: That year is remembered as the Year of Sorrow, or of Grief [Yaqeen].

screens.text: About ten years into the mission.

screens.text: **Guidance belongs to Allah.** He loved his uncle and longed for him to believe. The Qur'an reminded him that even he couldn't guide those he loved; guidance is Allah's to give [Q 28:56].

screens.text: **Love them, and leave guidance to Allah.** Loving family who don't share your faith is normal and right. The Prophet ﷺ did. Be kind, make **du'a** (personal prayer) for them, and remember their hearts are in Allah's hands, not yours.
bubbles: And grief is not weak faith. He grieved deeply that year, and he wept at other losses too [Bukhari 1303].

screens.situation: Luis has talked about Islam with his mom many times. She's kind about it, but she isn't interested. Luis feels like he's failing her.

options.text: Keep loving her, make du'a for her, and remember guidance is in Allah's hands
options.feedback: Yes. Even the Prophet ﷺ couldn't guide the uncle he loved. Luis's job is love and kindness [Q 28:56].

options.text: Bring it up at every visit until she gives in
options.feedback: Not quite. Pressure pushes people away. Kindness and du'a do more, and guidance is Allah's.

options.text: Stop visiting until she's ready to listen
options.feedback: Not quite. Keep the relationship warm. The Qur'an asks for kindness to parents [Q 31:15].

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Khadijah died about three years before the hijra [Bukhari 3896], after about 25 years of marriage [Qalam ep. 55; Yaqeen].
- His uncle Abu Talib died around the same time, about ten years into the mission [IslamQA 11575; IslamQA 20240]. Qalam (ep. 55–56) says the 11th year; say "about ten years in".
- At Abu Talib's deathbed the Prophet ﷺ urged him to say *la ilaha illa Allah*; he died on his forefathers' religion [Bukhari 3884; Bukhari 1360]. On screen we say only that he never accepted Islam, yet the Prophet ﷺ loved him.
- You cannot guide whom you love; Allah guides whom He wills [Q 28:56].
- With both gone, the persecution grew harsher [IslamQA 11575; Qalam ep. 56].

**Likely questions**
- *"Where is Abu Talib now?"* This is sensitive, especially for converts with non-Muslim parents. Answer gently and briefly: there are authentic hadith on this [Bukhari 3884; Bukhari 1360], and scholars discuss them. Don't deny the texts and don't speculate about any person. Stress that Allah alone judges, with perfect justice and mercy, and offer "Ask my imam". (scholar question Q42)
- *"Can I pray for my non-Muslim parents?"* For the living: yes, make du'a for their guidance and wellbeing, and treat them kindly [Q 31:14–15]. For a relative who has died, follow Day 77: state the Qur'an's guidance gently [Q 9:113], name what is open (grieving, attending the funeral, condolence, kindness), note that scholars discuss the details, and offer the imam. Never comment on any individual's fate. (scholar question Q23)
- *"Isn't Bukhari 3896 about Aisha's age?"* The report mentions it, and this episode cites it only for Khadijah's death. If asked, follow the track's approach: the sahih reports give six at the contract and nine when the marriage began [Bukhari 5133]; scholars discuss it; never mock the question or deny the hadith; offer the imam. (scholar question Q37)
- *"Is grief okay in Islam?"* Yes. He wept at his son's death and called it mercy [Bukhari 1303]. Point to Day 77 and Day 64.

**Escalate:** the afterlife of Abu Talib (Q42) or of the convert's own deceased relative (Q23); Aisha's age beyond the outline above (Q37); any convert in acute grief or crisis (safety rule if there's risk).

**Don't**
- Never raise Abu Talib's fate unless asked, and never on a screen.
- Don't quote Bukhari 3884 or 1360 word for word to someone grieving; summarise gently if asked.
- Don't use the convert's family to pressure them.
- Don't picture the Prophet ﷺ, Khadijah or Abu Talib.
